Q: How can I use parameters within a measure? A:

The above syntax should work, if you have created some numeric range parameters using the Modelling/New Parameter option. As noted in my comment it will return a blank if the parameter slicers are on another page to where the measure is placed, if the slicer are not synchronized.

In this example I have recreated your basic solution:

Two parameter slicers have been created, called 'Parameter' and 'Parameter 2', and contains two objects automatically create. The table of the integer range, and the measure that takes the selected value from the slicer. The table is created using a generate series uses the syntax of:

Parameter = GENERATESERIES(0, 20, 1)

Which creates a series from 0 to 20 in increments of 1. The 'Parameter Value' is a measure, that is created with the syntax of:

Parameter Value = SELECTEDVALUE('Parameter'[Parameter])

So using your code as a base for the summing of the two parameters values: With P1 = 4 and P2 = 5:

New Measure = VAR p1 = 'Parameter'[Parameter Value]
VAR p2 = 'Parameter 2'[Parameter Value 2]
RETURN p1 + p2

Yields the result of 9

In the case if it retuning blank, as mentioned in my comment, if your measure is on a separate page the slicer context isn't passed to that page, and you will have to use the option of 'synchronize Slicers' to apply slicers from one page to the others.

If you select the slicer object and in this case tick the Page 2 options, then the slicer will propagate to the page the measure is on. You can also choose to show the slicers on the other page or not in the Sync Slicers option. Example PBIX file 'SO_Question_76424090.pbix' is here

Q: Google Data Studio - Separating values within string A:

You can create your own customized Community Connector that will do this. In the connector code, this field will have to be parsed into separate fields. You can use split() to do that.

Q: Excel Pivot Chart: remove zero values A:

Found a trick: in the data field use =if(x=0,na(),x/y). The graph will be fine but the table will look ugly (with #NAs). You can use conditional formatting on the table to set the font color as white when there is an error.

Voila!!!

Q: How do I revive vibe code that was automated by Claude A:

What would you do if you weren't vibe coding? Hopefully the answer includes writing automated tests and working incrementally and iteratively.

When I'm building software, I do so in a test-driven manner. I don't want to write a ton of code in one go, as there's too much context to manage. Instead, writing a test first gives me one part of the problem to focus on. Also, I'm running all the tests frequently to ensure that the current changes aren't breaking existing functionality.
